translations.answer: The original implementation only modified static friction, while separate setters still overwrite group properties via set_dof_friction_properties, leading to static being below the retained dynamic value. The merged PR #3318 addresses static, dynamic, and viscous friction, restricting coefficients to non-negative and maintaining dynamic ≤ static; reviewed tests now validate PhysX buffer rather than internal Isaac Lab cache.
translations.applicability: Applies to Isaac Sim 5.0 and corresponding Isaac Lab domain randomization path; older versions may not support separate dynamic/viscous settings.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, environment is clear and non-conflicting, and there is formal documentation or independent reproducible exact reference.
translations.details.attempts.0: An attempt was submitted in the Issue comment to generate static/dynamic/viscous values, restrict to non-negative, and maintain dynamic ≤ static.
translations.details.attempts.1: PR #3318 was reviewed multiple times, modifying the test to validate the root_physx_view buffer instead of internal Isaac Lab data.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Simultaneously reads static, dynamic, and viscous joint friction properties, not just the randomized static value.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Checks if set_dof_friction_properties is re-writing group friction properties during continuous calls to write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim and dynamic setter.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Using an Isaac Lab version that includes merged PR #3318, joint parameters are randomized while handling static, dynamic (Coulomb), and viscous friction, and static ≥ dynamic is maintained.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab commit 9d6321463067c541ce1a24531ff87f99a18fd8f7; Isaac Sim 5.0; Ubuntu 22.04; NVIDIA L40S; CUDA 12.4; driver 550.107.02.
translations.details.limits.0: Initial submission had issues with CPU/CUDA device inconsistency and values not being written to simulator; subsequent patch addresses this.
translations.details.limits.1: During PR merging, 10 of 13 checks passed, but the original page did not show the status of the remaining 3; the target version should still run friction buffer comparison.
translations.details.limits.2: Original Issue addressed Isaac Sim 5.0's three friction APIs; older Isaac Sim versions must be handled per corresponding version.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #3318 merged into main on 2025-09-29; PR page shows merged commit 21bcb47, Issue closed on same day.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Final PR checked tests, documentation, and changelog, and during review, the friction assertion was changed to validate PhysX simulator buffer.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Isaac Lab's randomize_joint_parameters only modifies static friction, so how should static be handled when dynamic is greater?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Friction randomization range needs to be verified against real joints, lubrication, temperature, and actuator characteristics; satisfying PhysX mathematical constraints does not equate to parameter having physical realism.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Original implementation only randomized static friction; author confirmed that group properties are overwritten during separate writes.
translations.details.symptoms.0: static friction=10, dynamic friction=10; using 0.5–1.5 scale for static randomization, PhysX reports 'Static friction effort must be greater than or equal to dynamic friction effort.'
translations.source.locator: Isaac Lab #3266 minimal repro and issuecomment-3219603398/3219638763, merged PR #3318 and its PhysX buffer test review chain
